check-manifest-unsupported-pattern.reason: Adopt for #197 by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-18. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: check_manifest.py applied any pattern Python's re accepts, so ^(?=a) matched 'abc', exit 0. New behavior: bench-tools check-manifest supports the pyregex syntax (literals, ., ^, $, groups without ?, alternation, classes, \d \D \s \S \w \W \b \B, the common escapes, greedy and lazy quantifiers, and the global flags i, m, s, x and u at the start) and refuses every other pattern Python accepts, such as lookarounds, (?:...), named groups, backreferences, \A, \Z, scoped flags and (?a), with exit 2 and an unsupported-pattern message naming the pattern. Rationale: a bounded matcher with no registry dependency answers the schemas' patterns without a backtracking engine; refusing loudly keeps a schema from being read some other way. Compatibility impact: no repository schema uses any of them; `git ls-files '*.schema.json'` lists 33 schemas whose 29 distinct patterns all compile under pyregex. Resolving issue: #197.
